blocks.raw: # Configure Delivery Settings
blocks.text: Configure Delivery Settings

blocks.raw: ## Engagement channels sender details
blocks.text: Engagement channels sender details

blocks.raw: When you [create a campaign](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-campaign#/) and [add message](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-message#/), you select the [engagement channel](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/engagement-channels#/) through which the message will be delivered to your audience. Along with the channel, you also need to add the sender details. The sender details define the **Sender ID**, **Reply-to Id** and **Sender Name** that will be used to send the message.
blocks.text: When you create a campaign and add message, you select the engagement channel through which the message will be delivered to your audience. Along with the channel, you also need to add the sender details. The sender details define the Sender ID, Reply-to Id and Sender Name that will be used to send the message.

blocks.raw: To configure the domain gateway and sender details, create a ticket to the Capillary Gateway team. For more information refer to [Configure domain settings]()
blocks.text: To configure the domain gateway and sender details, create a ticket to the Capillary Gateway team. For more information refer to Configure domain settings

blocks.text: To add the sender details on the UI follow the given steps:

blocks.raw: 1. Create a campaign and then create a message, choose the desired engagement channel and navigate to **Delivery settings** and select **Show**.
blocks.text: Create a campaign and then create a message, choose the desired engagement channel and navigate to Delivery settings and select Show.

blocks.raw: ## Target DND users
blocks.text: Target DND users

blocks.raw: Mobile SMS messages are blocked for users who have marked themselves as **DND (Do Not Disturb)**. By default, messages are not sent to DND users, but you can manually enable messaging for them if required. This is useful for checking reachability if those DND users have opted out of DND.
blocks.text: Mobile SMS messages are blocked for users who have marked themselves as DND (Do Not Disturb). By default, messages are not sent to DND users, but you can manually enable messaging for them if required. This is useful for checking reachability if those DND users have opted out of DND.

blocks.raw: To allow messages to be sent to DND users:
blocks.text: To allow messages to be sent to DND users:

blocks.raw: * Enable the **NDNC** toggle to send messages to customers subscribed to DND.
blocks.text: Enable the NDNC toggle to send messages to customers subscribed to DND.

blocks.raw: By default, this option is **not available** for all organisations. To enable it, navigate to `_{hostURL}orgadmin/administer/{orgID}_ `and enable the **Send to NDNC Customer** option.
blocks.text: By default, this option is not available for all organisations. To enable it, navigate to _{hostURL}orgadmin/administer/{orgID}_ and enable the Send to NDNC Customer option.

blocks.raw: ## Send communication to control customers
blocks.text: Send communication to control customers

blocks.raw: In general, Test Audience/Customers are the selected group of customers or audience to whom all communication messages are sent. Control Audience/Customers are the selected group of customers or audience for whom messages are not sent. The brand decides the ratio and group of the Test-Control audience.
blocks.text: In general, Test Audience/Customers are the selected group of customers or audience to whom all communication messages are sent. Control Audience/Customers are the selected group of customers or audience for whom messages are not sent. The brand decides the ratio and group of the Test-Control audience.

blocks.raw: By default, the campaign communication messages are not sent to the Control customers but only to the Test customers. You can turn on the toggle switch to enable sending communications to Control customers.
blocks.text: By default, the campaign communication messages are not sent to the Control customers but only to the Test customers. You can turn on the toggle switch to enable sending communications to Control customers.

blocks.raw: ## Send messages to unsubscribed users
blocks.text: Send messages to unsubscribed users

blocks.raw: This feature enables you to send communication messages to customers who have disabled their subscription status. You can set this while configuring the campaign or journey.
blocks.text: This feature enables you to send communication messages to customers who have disabled their subscription status. You can set this while configuring the campaign or journey.

blocks.raw: When this option is enabled, users who have unsubscribed from a channel are not filtered out from your audience. They will receive the communication if they are reachable on the selected channel.
blocks.text: When this option is enabled, users who have unsubscribed from a channel are not filtered out from your audience. They will receive the communication if they are reachable on the selected channel.

blocks.raw: **Note**: Use this option only when your use case requires reaching all contactable users, including those who have unsubscribed.
blocks.text: Note: Use this option only when your use case requires reaching all contactable users, including those who have unsubscribed.

blocks.raw: ## Shortening URLs in communication messages
blocks.text: Shortening URLs in communication messages

blocks.raw: This helps you shorten any URL in your communication message when you are constrained by character limits. You can enable **Use tiny URL** from the delivery settings, and the system will automatically shorten the URL. This is applicable across all <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/engagement-channels#/">engagement channels</Anchor>.
blocks.text: This helps you shorten any URL in your communication message when you are constrained by character limits. You can enable Use tiny URL from the delivery settings, and the system will automatically shorten the URL. This is applicable across all engagement channels.
